definition: In this source, special needs refers to a child or other individual whose care requires extra support and ongoing attention beyond usual family routines. The term is used socially to describe circumstances that can increase caregiver responsibilities and burden, affecting parents’ time, social life, and ability to do other activities.

reasons: The definition’s claim that “special needs” refers to a “child or other individual whose care requires extra support and ongoing attention beyond usual family routines” is not explicitly stated in the packet text.

While the packet discusses “parents caring for individuals with special needs,” “families plan their entire lives around their children’s needs,” and neglecting “social lives and free time” (supporting ideas about social life/time burden), it does not define the term as a general social label used to describe “extra support” or “ongoing attention beyond usual family routines.”

The packet’s content supports discussing challenges, care burden, and barriers associated with having a child with special needs, but the provided definition introduces wording (“extra support and ongoing attention beyond usual family routines,” “used socially to describe circumstances”) that is not directly supported by the supplied source text.
